alt: Surgically targeted clinical Independent Medical Review (IMR) complaint filed with the California DMHC, demanding an expedited, directed clinical referral to an in-network or out-of-network physician to supervise a high-risk benzodiazepine taper.
full_text: Severe physiological benzodiazepine dependence requiring a strictly managed, medically supervised titration and clinical taper. Patient faces an immediate, documented risk of acute central nervous system destabilization, acute withdrawal syndrome, and life-threatening complications, including seizures, if unsupervised. Immediate authorization for an expedited, directed clinical referral to a qualified provider (in-network or out-of-network) for mandatory physician oversight, monitoring, and clinical management of a high-risk medical taper. Requesting immediate network placement with a supervising physician to prevent severe neurological complications. Urgent/Expedited IMR request for immediate threat to safety. Health plan constructively denied care and failed its statutory duty to provide a network physician to manage a high-risk psychiatric taper. Patient is undergoing a medical taper from long-term benzodiazepines due to physiological dependence. As certified by the specialist, unmonitored titration presents an immediate risk of acute CNS destabilization, severe withdrawal, and life-threatening grand mal seizures. To avoid severe danger, patient sought emergency out-of-network care out-of-pocket. Provider issued a final 30-day prescription on June 8, 2026, and canceled the subscription. Patient faces a total loss of medical supervision in under 30 days while mid-taper.
summary: Surgically targeted clinical Independent Medical Review (IMR) complaint filed directly with the DMHC. This filing demands immediate, forward-looking network placement to prevent medical abandonment during a high-risk benzodiazepine taper, which the DMHC's intake caseworkers erroneously merged and diluted into an administrative consumer complaint.
